turns.text: Please help me plan the first month with a new car. I bought a 2019 blue hatchback from a Tamsen lot this morning, $14,200 financed. It replaces the old minivan, which I still need to sell or scrap. I want a numbered plan covering the budget, insurance and registration steps, and my schedule.

Congratulations on the new car. Here is a first-month plan.

1) This weekend: Confirm the paperwork. Keep the bill of sale, loan contract and title or title-transfer papers together in one folder.
2) Before you drive it much more: Insurance. Call your insurer or agent, add the hatchback by VIN, and ask for proof of coverage. Lenders usually require full coverage with comprehensive and collision. Ask what deductible you can afford.
3) Within the week: Take the old van off the policy only after it is sold or scrapped, and ask whether it can be pared down to minimal coverage until then.
4) Registration: Dealers often file title and registration paperwork, but confirm that. Ask the lot what they submitted, whether you will get temporary plates or a receipt, and when to expect the permanent registration. Check your state DMV's deadline for transfers.
5) The old van: Decide to sell or scrap. Gather the title, remove the plates if your state requires it, and file a release of liability so you are not responsible for it once it's gone.
6) Budget: Send me the monthly numbers you want to work with and I can build a table. What is your payment, and when does it start?

1) The payment is $318 a month for 48 months. First payment is due Nov 15. Fit it into the household budget.
2) I fill up at the Ruel Road station for the 30 cents savings. Include fuel in the monthly numbers.
3) Insurance quote not yet known.

Also. After Isabel's counselor meeting I ran the net price calculators myself and was surprised by the aid numbers. I do not want opinions about the car. Give me figures first, like that.

Figures first. Some inputs are missing, so I've used placeholders you can fill in.

Monthly car cost
- Loan payment: $318 x 48 months = $15,264 total payments. Against $14,200 financed, that is about $1,064 in total interest and fees.
- Fuel: [miles per month] ÷ [mpg] x [price per gallon]. Filling at the Ruel Road station at 30 cents a gallon less than elsewhere saves 30 cents x [gallons per month]. At 12 gallons a month that is $3.60; at 25 gallons it is $7.50.
- Insurance: [quote] per month. Get at least 3 quotes with the same coverage limits and deductible.
- Registration and fees: [annual amount] ÷ 12.
- Maintenance set-aside: a common rule is $40 to $60 a month for a used car.

Total monthly = $318 + fuel + insurance + [registration ÷ 12] + maintenance.

Timeline
1) Nov 15: first payment due. Set up autopay a few days earlier, and confirm the date and amount.
2) Before then: open your budget and add the total above as a fixed line.

Send me the insurance quote, your estimated monthly mileage and your mpg and I will replace the placeholders.

Now the schedule. I need the car sorted around my 5:45 a.m. Tuesday and Thursday walks on the boardwalk with Dana. That moved my evenings free for my mother. School is a four-minute drive and I arrive at 7:20. Numbered, short.

1) Mon night: Check gas level and keep your keys, phone and thermos by the door.
2) Tue/Thu 5:35: Leave for the boardwalk walk with Dana. Park, lock the car, and keep the car's paperwork out of sight.
3) Tue/Thu 6:45: Back home, quick reset, then leave for school.
4) Daily 7:20: Arrive at school ahead of the drop-off line.
5) Weekly: Fill up on the Ruel Road trip you already make. Set a phone reminder so it is done before the walk mornings.
6) Evenings: Use the freed time for your mother and for one car task per week, such as an insurance call, DMV check or listing the minivan.
7) Week 1: Call insurers. Week 2: Confirm registration status. Week 3: Sell or scrap the van. Week 4: Review actual costs against the budget table.

Want the van sale checklist next?

Van sale checklist:

1) Find the title. If it's missing, request a duplicate.
2) Note the mileage and any known problems; be honest in the listing.
3) Get quotes: a scrap yard, a used-car buyer, and one private listing.
4) Compare the payouts against the cost of any needed repairs.
5) At sale: sign the title, write a bill of sale, and take a photo of both.
6) File a release of liability with your state DMV.
7) Cancel or adjust the old policy only after the sale is done.
